requirement:
TOML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a value on the same line. A `#` inside a quoted
string belongs to the string.
rationale:
The `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.attachments` requirement is checked by the TOML case in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. That test carries a `{test}` reference to the requirement. I judged it from the test text alone and did not read the implementation.

The TOML source in that case is `# first\n# second\na = '# literal' # real\n"# key" = """# literal"""\n`. The test builds the outline with `OutlineContent::from_source`. It collects every attachment on every item, sorts them by span start, and compares the full `(kind, text)` list with `assert_eq!`. The expected list is `[(Comment, "# first"), (Comment, "# second"), (Comment, "# real")]`.

Each obligation maps to an assertion as follows:
- **Only `Comment` attachments.** The expected list contains only `Comment` kinds. Because the comparison is exact, any extra attachment of another kind, or of any kind, would fail it.
- **Each `#` comment is one attachment.** `# first` and `# second` are consecutive comment lines. They must come back as two separate attachments, not one merged one.
- **A trailing comment after a value on the same line.** `a = '# literal' # real` must yield `# real` as its own attachment.
- **A `#` inside a quoted string belongs to the string.** Three strings are covered:
  - The literal string `'# literal'` must not yield a comment.
  - The quoted key `"# key"` must not yield a comment.
  - The multi-line basic string `"""# literal"""` must not yield a comment.
  The exact-list comparison fails if any of these is reported as a comment.

The test does not use a plain single-line basic string as a value, a multi-line literal `'''` string, or escaped quotes. The requirement text does not distinguish these from the string forms already tested. The quoted key covers the basic-string `"` delimiter, and the exact-match assertion would catch any spurious comment. I found no obligation in the requirement text without a test, and no assertion that contradicts it.
